record.original_question: For planar polynomial differential systems of degree n >= 4, determine the maximum possible number C_n of centers.

evidence.quote: Problem 10. Determine the maximum number of centers, Cn, for planar polynomial differential systems of degree n >= 4.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A planar polynomial differential system of degree $n$ is a system of ordinary differential equations of the form
$$\dot x = P(x,y), \qquad \dot y = Q(x,y),$$
where $P, Q \in \mathbb{R}[x,y]$ and $\max\{\deg P, \deg Q\} = n$. A singular point $p_0 = (x_0,y_0)$ (i.e., $P(p_0)=Q(p_0)=0$) is called a center if there exists an open neighborhood $U$ of $p_0$ such that $U \setminus \{p_0\}$ is entirely filled with periodic orbits of the system.

For each integer $n \ge 4$, let
$$C_n = \sup\bigl\{\,\#\{\text{centers of }(P,Q)\} : (P,Q)\text{ is a planar polynomial system of degree }n\,\bigr\}.$$

Determine the value of $C_n$ for every $n \ge 4$.
artifact.category_tag: Centers of planar polynomial vector fields
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of determining the maximum number of centers $C_n$ for planar polynomial differential systems of degree $n \ge 4$ appears to remain open. Partial results exist for restricted subclasses (e.g., quartic Kolmogorov systems, where the maximum is seven, and certain cubic Kolmogorov classes), and constructions of families with many centers are known (e.g., new families of centers in arbitrary even degree), but no closed-form value of $C_n$ for general $n \ge 4$ has been established.

status_evidence.title: The maximum number of centers for planar polynomial Kolmogorov differential systems
status_evidence.snippet: The maximum number of centers is determined for planar quartic Kolmogorov polynomial differential systems (a restricted subclass).
status_evidence.claim: Only restricted subclasses (Kolmogorov systems) have a known maximum number of centers; the general case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Configuration of planar Kolmogorov cubic polynomial differential systems with the most centers
status_evidence.snippet: Studies maximum number of centers in cubic Kolmogorov systems.
status_evidence.claim: Results exist only for specific subclasses, supporting that the general problem for n>=4 is unsolved.

status_evidence.title: New Family of Centers of Planar Polynomial Differential Systems of Arbitrary Even Degree
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs new families with many centers in arbitrary even degree.
status_evidence.claim: Lower-bound constructions are known but no general formula for C_n.
